newsitem.title: POLAND: POLAND SAYS RAUTAKIRJA MAY BE IN RUCH BID.
newsitem.headline: POLAND SAYS RAUTAKIRJA MAY BE IN RUCH BID.

text.p: The Polish treasury ministry has shortlisted two entities bidding for a 75-percent stake in newsstand chain Ruch SA, a ministry spokesman told the daily Parkiet in its Tuesday edition.
"The so-called shortlist of bidders for the purchase of Ruch has been prepared," Zbigniew Ostrowski was quoted as saying.

The daily Rzeczpospolita cited unofficial sources in saying that one of the two bidders was Polish group Polska Grupa Kapitalowa, led by Universal and including private television Polsat SA and soft drink producer Multico SA.

Rzeczpospolita said the other was private printing house Uniprom, which was bidding for Ruch alone but which would cooperate with current Finnish partner Rautakirja on organising the chain should it win the bid.
Rzeczpospolita said Rautakirja had bid for Ruch when Poland called a first tender for the chain in 1995.
It said the whole process of selling Ruch might be completed by the end of June. The bidders would be able to see full details of the chain by mid-May and then submit final offers.

The ministry launched a new tender for the privatisation of Ruch, which controls 65 percent of Poland's press distribution market, in March after withdrawing from a nearly-done deal with a consortium led by French Hachette Distribution Service.
The Polish group, saying it would offer $80 million for a 40-percent stake in Ruch and pledging to invest a total of $200 million in the company, placed its bid in the new tender.
The daily Gazeta Wyborcza reported quoted anonymous sources earlier this month as saying that Germany's Bertelsmann AG had been interested in buying Ruch.
Hachette, which ignored the new tender, plans to create its own distribution network in Poland if the government fails to sell it Ruch.
